info.title: Maze API
info.description: The Maze API lets you pull vulnerability investigation data out of Maze into your own systems. Authenticate with an API key in the `X-API-Key` header.

post.description: Returns investigations for your organization, ordered by `updated_at` ascending.

example.detail: Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.

get.description:
Returns the most recent daily investigation export files for your organization, newest first, up to 14 entries.

Each export is a delta: all investigations whose `updated_at` timestamp falls within that calendar day (UTC). Apply deltas in order to keep your own data store in sync. If an investigation appears in multiple deltas it was updated on multiple days — use the latest record.

Export files are generated daily. When `format` is `jsonl.gz`, the file is JSONL gzip: each line is one investigation object with the same schema as items returned by `POST /v1/investigations/search`.

example.detail: Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.

get.description:
Returns details and a time-limited signed download URL (1-minute TTL) for a specific daily investigation export file.

When `format` is `jsonl.gz`, the file is JSONL gzip: each line is one investigation object with the same schema as items returned by `POST /v1/investigations/search`.

No `download_url` is returned when `status` is `empty` or `unavailable`.

example.detail: Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.

get.description:
**Beta.** Returns your organization's most recent FedRAMP deviation exports, newest first, up to 20 entries.

Metadata only. Read one export to get its download URLs.

example.detail: Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.

post.description:
**Beta.** Starts a FedRAMP deviation export for one calendar day and returns the export to poll.

Returns `202` while the export is being produced, and `200` when an export for that day has already finished. Either way the `export_id` is the same for a given day: asking twice joins the export already running rather than starting a second one, and never renumbers a deviation request.

Download URLs are not returned here. Poll `GET /v1/reports/fedramp/exports/{export_id}` until `status` is `available`, then read `artifacts`.

One export runs at a time per organization: while one is `pending`, creating an export for a different day returns `409`. A day that has already finished is still returned, since that starts no work. A run that failed can be created again to retry it.

200.description: An export for this day has already finished.

example.detail: Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.

get.description:
**Beta.** Returns one export and, once `status` is `available`, a time-limited signed download URL per file (1-minute TTL).

Both files hold the same records: `jsonl` is one deviation record per line, `jsonl.gz` is that file gzipped. Each carries a `sha256` to verify the download.

Every record names its kind in `deviation_type`. Read that field rather than assuming an export holds a single kind.

`artifacts` is empty while the export is `pending`, when it is `empty`, and when it is `unavailable`.

cve_id.title: Cve Id
cve_id.description: CVE identifier this investigation was run against.

scanner_finding_hash.title: Scanner Finding Hash
scanner_finding_hash.description: Maze's deduplication hash for this finding, computed from the scanner finding hash combined with orchestration context.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent pipeline output change (always UTC). Advances when exploitability, likelihood, impact, severity, root cause analysis, or remediation outputs change. CVE metadata (see `snapshot`) can change without advancing this field.

exploitability.title: Exploitability
exploitability.description: Exploitability verdict for this asset/CVE pair. 'exploitable': the CVE is actively exploitable on this asset. 'not_exploitable': the CVE cannot be triggered on this asset (includes cases where exploitability could not be conclusively determined).

exploitability_reason.title: Exploitability Reason
exploitability_reason.description: Short explanation for the exploitability verdict, drawn from the LLM analysis output.

likelihood.description: Likelihood score: estimated probability that this vulnerability leads to a security incident on this asset. Null when the assessment was skipped or inconclusive.

impact.description: Impact score: estimated severity of damage if this vulnerability is successfully exploited. Null when the assessment was skipped or inconclusive.

likelihood_assessment.title: Likelihood Assessment
likelihood_assessment.description: Full structured output from the likelihood assessment agent, including reasoning, evidence, and intermediate conclusions. Null when no likelihood assessment has been produced.

impact_assessment.title: Impact Assessment
impact_assessment.description: Full structured output from the impact assessment agent, including reasoning, evidence, and intermediate conclusions. Null when no impact assessment has been produced.

maze_severity.description: Overall Maze risk score combining exploitability, likelihood, and impact. 'NOT_EXPLOITABLE' when the CVE cannot be exploited on this asset.

vulnerability_root_cause_analysis.title: Vulnerability Root Cause Analysis
vulnerability_root_cause_analysis.description: Structured root cause analysis identifying the conditions that make this asset vulnerable. Each item describes one root cause factor.

investigation_steps.title: Investigation Steps
investigation_steps.description: Ordered steps the AI investigator took to reach its exploitability verdict.

severity_details.description: Human-readable explanation for the severity assessment, including the reasoning narrative and the specific factors that drove the score.

related_scanner_findings.title: Related Scanner Findings
related_scanner_findings.description: Scanner findings covered by this investigation. A single investigation may cover multiple findings when the same CVE affects the same asset across different scanners or orchestration contexts.

snapshot.description: CVE context snapshot. May be silently updated when NVD refreshes CVSS scores or Maze re-generates CVE summaries, without advancing `updated_at`.

updated_from.title: Updated From
updated_from.description: Return investigations with `updated_at` at or after this time (ISO 8601). Timezone-naive values are treated as UTC.

updated_to.title: Updated To
updated_to.description: Return investigations with `updated_at` before this time (ISO 8601). Timezone-naive values are treated as UTC.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass this value as `cursor` to retrieve the next page. Null when there are no more results.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether more results exist beyond this page.

status.title: Status
status.description: Current finding status. Updated by users or automation independently of the investigation pipeline.

status_reason.title: Status Reason
status_reason.description: Reason recorded with the most recent status transition.

cve.description: CVE text fields for this investigation.

InvestigationSnapshotResponse.title: InvestigationSnapshotResponse
InvestigationSnapshotResponse.description:
Fields that may change without advancing `updated_at`.

These reflect current state from sources outside the investigation pipeline:
CVE data from NVD, and finding status from user/automation actions. If you
are syncing by `updated_at`, treat this object as a best-effort current view
rather than a point-in-time pipeline output.

tags.name: Investigations
tags.description:
Query and export investigation data.

**Search** — filter and paginate investigations in real time. Use `updated_from` for incremental sync.

**Daily exports** — download JSONL.gz delta files, one per UTC day. Apply in order; keep the latest version of each investigation.

tags.name: FedRAMP (Beta)
tags.description:
Produce and download FedRAMP deviation exports.

Create an export for a calendar day, poll it, then download the JSONL and JSONL.gz files through signed URLs.

An export carries the deviation requests Maze has determined for your organization, each record naming its kind in `deviation_type`. Maze adds kinds over time, so treat that set as open and filter on the field rather than on the export.

**Beta** — available to organizations with FedRAMP reporting enabled. The shape of these endpoints may still change.
